stem.text: A beam of light consists of two wavelengths of $436\,\text{nm}$ and $654\,\text{nm}$. A diffraction grating of $5.00 \times 10^{5}\,\text{lines m}^{-1}$ produces a diffraction pattern in which the second order of one of these wavelengths occurs at the same angle $\theta$ as the third order of the other wavelength.

stem.alt: Beam of light labelled 436 nm and 654 nm passing through a diffraction grating, with zero order, overlapping orders and angle θ labelled on both sides of the normal.
